brief: One drawer and one spike, both at the very same corner of the same cell, touching.

requirements.evidence: drawer:0#0,0#cut sits on the cut face of the north half base piece:0,0,0;half-n.
spike:0#0,-1|0,0|1,-1 stands where cells 0,0, 0,-1 and 1,-1 meet.

requirements.requirement: Drawer and spike at the very same corner of the same cell, touching
requirements.evidence: The configurator refuses this with SPIKE_CLASH: the drawer fills the corner where the spike would stand. That happened at both corners at the drawer's end and at the east corner on the cut line. The spike is on a north corner of the same cell instead and doesn't touch the drawer.

finish.summary: I couldn't put the drawer and the spike at the same corner of one cell. The configurator refuses it: when the drawer was in place, both corners at the drawer's end were refused with SPIKE_CLASH ("a drawer fills this corner of the junction"). The east corner on the cut line was refused the same way, and I didn't try the west corner. A drawer needs a half base, so I turned cell 0,0 into a north half base (half-n) and set the drawer (drawer:0#0,0#cut) in its south half. A spike can only stand where three cells meet, so I added cells 0,-1 and 1,-1 and put the spike (spike:0#0,-1|0,0|1,-1) at the north-east corner of cell 0,0. That corner is the far side of the same cell from the drawer, so the two don't touch. Open faces are capped and the joints bolted. check_build found no rule issues and no mesh clashes.

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
